buttons.description: Read starting values off this measurement: the crosstalk from where the donor-only population sits, the donor lifetime from its mean micro time, the donor-only fraction from its share of the bursts, and one distance per state spread over the FRET population. Use it when a fit has settled somewhere that plainly does not describe the data — six free parameters over a multi-modal objective end up where their start point's basin takes them. Parameters you have fixed are left alone.

sections.description: One row per exchanging state: its mean donor-acceptor distance in Angstrom, and its equilibrium population. Adding or removing a state resizes the rate matrix with it.
sections.title: states

sections.description: The donor-only fraction does not take part in the exchange: a molecule with no active acceptor has no FRET state to be in.
sections.title: states — bounds and errors
Rate matrix
sections.description: Exchange rates between states, in inverse seconds. **Leave every rate at zero for a static analysis** — an empty scheme is exactly the static mixture, so one model covers both and you do not have to choose before the data has told you which it is. A rate far below one transition per burst is indistinguishable from static; far above it, the states merge into one averaged population; between the two, bursts caught mid-exchange fill the space between the states and pull the cloud off the static line, which is the signal being fitted.
Correction factors and dye constants. All of them act inside the forward model, never on the data histogram, which is what lets any of them be freed without the fit's target moving underneath it.
